events.title: Vasco da Gama Departs Lisbon for India
events.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama set sail from Lisbon with four ships on a voyage to find a sea route to India around the Cape of Good Hope.
events.significance: The voyage opened the first direct maritime trade route between Europe and Asia, reshaping global trade and establishing Portugal as a major colonial and commercial power.

events.title: First Public Reading of the Declaration of Independence
events.description: Colonel John Nixon gave the first public reading of the Declaration of Independence to a crowd in Philadelphia's Independence Square, and the Liberty Bell was rung to mark the occasion.
events.significance: The reading spread the news of American independence to the public and helped rally support for the revolutionary cause.

events.title: Commodore Perry Arrives in Edo Bay
events.description: U.S. Navy Commodore Matthew C. Perry arrived in Edo Bay, Japan, with a squadron of four warships, seeking to open Japan to trade with the West.
events.significance: Perry's expedition ended over two centuries of Japanese isolation, leading to the Convention of Kanagawa in 1854 and setting Japan on the path to modernization.

events.title: Birth of John D. Rockefeller
events.description: John Davison Rockefeller, founder of Standard Oil, was born in Richford, New York.
events.significance: Rockefeller became one of the wealthiest people in modern history, transformed the oil industry, and became a major philanthropist whose gifts helped establish institutions in education and medicine.

events.title: Death of Kim Il-sung
events.description: Kim Il-sung, the founding leader of North Korea, died of a heart attack at age 82 after ruling the country since 1948.
events.significance: His death led to the first hereditary transfer of power in a communist state, as his son Kim Jong-il took over, establishing a dynasty that continues to shape East Asian geopolitics.
